Counsel for Applicant :- Karm Veer Yadav

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Vidyarthi,J.
1.
Heard Sri Karm Veer Yadav, the learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Sanjay Maurya, the learned AGA for the State and perused the records.

2. By means of the instant application filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C., the applicants have sought quashing of order dated 17.07.2023 passed by the Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Ayodhya/Faizabad in Complaint Case No. 17/2019 filed by the opposite party no. 2, whereby the applicants have been summoned to face trial.

3. In the complaint lodged on 22.08.2019, the opposite party no. 2 had stated that he was getting a latrine constructed and the applicants abused and beaten him up so as to restrain him from constructing the latrine.
He further stated that he has approached the police with a complaint.
The police got him medically examined but his FIR was not registered.

It was further stated in the complaint that he had filed an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C., which was rejected and a Ramesh Singh Chauhan And 3 Others vs State Of U.P. Thru. Its Prin. Secy. ...

4.

The learned counsel for the applicants has submitted that the complaint has been filed on 22.08.2019 whereas the occurrence allegedly took place on 24.03.2018 and that the complaint has been filed after rejection of the complaint under Section 156(3) and dismissal of the revision filed against that order, which renders the complaint and summoning order passed in furtherance thereof liable to be quashed.
5. He has further submitted that on 24.03.2018, proceedings under Sections 151/ 107/ 116 IPC were drawn against the complainant Kali Prasad and one Ram Anjor.

The reports submitted under Sections 151/107/116 IPC against the applicant and Ram Anjor mentions that a quarrel had taken place between Ram Anjor and the opposite party no. 2 regarding some property dispute.

The mere occurrence of a quarrel between the opposite party no. 2 and some other person would not give rise to a presumption that the allegations levelled in the complaint, which are supported by the statements recorded under Sections 202 & 202 Cr.P.C., are false.
The correctness of the allegations has to be decided by the trial court after the parties lead their respective evidences.

6. So far as the submissions regarding the complaint having been filed after rejection of the complaint under Sections 156(3) is concerned, that application had been filed with request of lodging report.

The application under Sections 156(3) was rejected after noting that the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held in Smt. Priyanka Srivastava & Ors. v. State of U.P. & Ors, Criminal Appeal No. 781 of 2012 that there has to be prior application under Section 154(1) and 154(3) while filing petition under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.

entities.text: Priyanka Srivastava & Ors. v. State of U.P. & Ors, Criminal Appeal No. 781 of 2012
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Both the aspects should be clearly spelt out in the application and necessary documents to that effect should be filed.

The Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Faizabad had rejected the application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. on the ground that the applicant had not complied with the aforesaid mandate of law.
7. In such circumstances, the rejection of application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. will not create a bar against filing of a complaint.
8. Accordingly, the application lacks merit and the same is hereby dismissed.
